claim: Contrast-Consistent Search (CCS), an unsupervised linear-probe method using only logical-consistency constraints on activations, recovers a model's latent truth judgments that outperform the model's own zero-shot-generated answers by 4% accuracy on average across 6 models and 10 datasets.
stance_target: probes on internal activations can be more reliable/accurate than the model's own verbalized outputs
scope_conditions: General QA/true-false/sentiment-as-truth benchmarks across 6 models, 10 datasets; whole-statement binary truth granularity; non-code
quoted_support: across 6 models and 10 question-answering datasets, it outperforms zero-shot accuracy by 4% on average.

claim: The CCS probe remains accurate even when the model is deliberately prompted to generate incorrect answers, and it halves prompt sensitivity relative to reading answers off the model's stated output.
stance_target: internal probes are robust to surface-level manipulation/prompting that corrupts the model's verbalized output
scope_conditions: General QA benchmarks; adversarial-prompting robustness tests
quoted_support: it cuts prompt sensitivity in half and continues to maintain high accuracy even when models are prompted to generate incorrect answers.

claim: Burns et al. explicitly frame their contribution as an initial step toward discovering what a language model knows as distinct from what it says, using zero supervision and no access to explicit ground-truth labels -- but at whole-statement binary-truth granularity in non-code QA/commonsense domains, using an unsupervised contrastive-consistency method rather than a supervised per-requirement correctness classifier trained against unit-test labels.
stance_target: does this paper scoop per-requirement code-correctness probe-vs-verbalization gap?
scope_conditions: Comparison of CCS's scope (general QA, whole-claim, unsupervised) against the proposed AAAI-27 pivot (code, per-requirement, supervised probe trained against unit-test pass/fail labels, contrasted with trained self-reported confidence)
quoted_support: Our results provide an initial step toward discovering what language models know, distinct from what they say, even when we don't have access to explicit ground truth labels.
